about: The thirty niche showcase storyboards in examples/niches: what each is, and the brief it was written from. Written by an AI model from the brief; everything after the storyboard is made locally.

entries.title: What is a cookie, really?
entries.brief: A 40-second explainer of web cookies for people who only know the banner: what they are, how a login uses one, first party versus third party, and how to control them.

entries.title: The padlock in your browser, explained
entries.brief: A 45-second explainer of HTTPS: what the padlock means, how a secure connection starts, what a certificate authority does, and what the padlock does not tell you.

entries.title: Why phone batteries age
entries.brief: A 35-second explainer of lithium-ion battery wear, with what speeds it up, what helps, and a reminder not to obsess.

entries.title: Undo your last git commit
entries.brief: A 45-second git tip: three ways to undo the last commit with reset, and when to use revert instead because the commit was already pushed.

entries.title: Flatten your code with early returns
entries.brief: A 40-second coding tip: replace nested if blocks with early returns, shown as a before and after in JavaScript.

entries.title: Name your booleans like questions
entries.brief: A 35-second naming tip: booleans should read like yes or no questions, with is, has, can and should prefixes, and no double negatives.

entries.title: The rule of 72
entries.brief: A 40-second explainer of the rule of 72 for estimating how long money takes to double, with a chart for four rates and a clear 'not advice' ending.

entries.title: What is an index fund?
entries.brief: A 45-second explainer of index funds: what an index is, how a fund tracks it, how it compares with one stock, and that it is not risk-free.

entries.title: Why $100 buys less every year
entries.brief: A 35-second explainer of inflation with an illustrative chart: what $100 is worth after ten and twenty years at three percent a year.

entries.title: Why you stopped getting stronger
entries.brief: A 40-second explainer of progressive overload with four simple levers and a safety note.

entries.title: How much exercise do adults need?
entries.brief: A 45-second summary of the World Health Organization's activity guidance for adults, with the numbers on screen.

entries.title: Sleep is part of training
entries.brief: A 35-second note that recovery includes sleep, with the CDC's hours for adults and four habits that help.

entries.title: The stone that unlocked Egypt
entries.brief: A 45-second history of the Rosetta Stone: the decree, the three scripts, the find in 1799 and the decipherment in 1822.

entries.title: London burns, 1666
entries.brief: A 45-second account of the Great Fire of London with the timeline, the scale, and the rebuilding.

entries.title: The machine that changed reading
entries.brief: A 40-second history of Gutenberg's printing press: hand-copied books, movable type, and how quickly presses spread.

entries.title: The two-minute rule
entries.brief: A 35-second explainer of the two-minute rule from Getting Things Done, with examples and its limits.

entries.title: Beat procrastination with a timer
entries.brief: A 35-second explainer of the Pomodoro Technique with its steps and origin.

entries.title: Urgent or important?
entries.brief: A 45-second explainer of the Eisenhower matrix with its four quadrants.

entries.title: Meet Lumen: light that follows the day
entries.brief: A 35-second launch video for a fictional desk lamp called Lumen. Clearly a sample: it shows what a product launch can look like and names no real company.

entries.title: Tally: notes with no account
entries.brief: A 35-second launch video for a fictional notes app called Tally. A sample, naming no real company.

entries.title: Trailmix: a boot made for wet rock
entries.brief: A 40-second launch video for a fictional hiking boot called Trailmix. A sample, naming no real company.

entries.title: Ser or estar?
entries.brief: A 40-second Spanish tip on ser versus estar with examples and the DOCTOR and PLACE memory trick.

entries.title: Japanese uses three writing systems at once
entries.brief: A 45-second overview of hiragana, katakana, kanji and romaji.

entries.title: One syllable, four meanings: Mandarin tones
entries.brief: A 35-second introduction to the four Mandarin tones using the syllable ma.

entries.title: Why do we have seasons?
entries.brief: A 45-second explainer of seasons: axial tilt, not distance from the Sun.

entries.title: How a vaccine teaches your body
entries.brief: A 40-second explainer of how vaccines train the immune system.

entries.title: A year that measures distance: the light-year
entries.brief: A 35-second explainer of the light-year with the nearest star.

entries.title: Frankenstein in a minute
entries.brief: A 45-second summary of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein (1818), with one real quotation from the book.

entries.title: The Art of War in a minute
entries.brief: A 45-second summary of The Art of War, traditionally credited to Sun Tzu.

entries.title: A Roman emperor's private notes: Meditations
entries.brief: A 40-second summary of Marcus Aurelius's Meditations and its Stoic themes.
